source.title: PreFLMR: Scaling Up Fine-Grained Late-Interaction Multi-modal Retrievers
source.authors: Weizhe Lin; Jing-Biao Mei; Jinghong Chen; Bill Byrne

record.tranche_reason: The paper varies model-component size and reports retrieval performance, testing whether downstream performance changes with scale using a different model family and metric. It does not test language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper studies multimodal retrieval performance as vision and text encoders are scaled, plus text-only retrieval during encoder pre-training. It does not fit power laws or test parameter-token-compute trade-offs. Rows therefore bear on V6's downstream-performance-with-scale wording, not on cross-entropy scaling or power-law form. Other retrieval comparisons and ablations are outside the claim versions.
record.test_reason: A new setting: multimodal late-interaction retrieval. The paper scales pretrained text encoders (BERT/ColBERT) and vision encoders (ViT-B to ViT-G) and reports retrieval-task performance at each size. That bears on V6's 'downstream performance improves with scale', and only on that. No loss curves, power-law fits or compute trade-offs are reported, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested. Because no fits are made, V6's 'predictably' is tested only as the direction of change across a few sizes.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that scaling the vision encoder from ViT-B to ViT-G gives substantial gains, largest from B to L, with a plateau at H/G. A text encoder beyond BERT-base (110M) is not needed for multimodal retrieval: Large-v1 hurt because it overfit and trained unstably, though it helped in text-only ColBERT training. Scaling the mapping structure does not help. They make no power-law or loss-scaling claim.
record.recipe_differences: This is a multimodal retrieval scaling study using encoder-size comparisons and retrieval metrics, rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy sweeps across parameters, tokens, and compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Results depend on which component is scaled: vision scaling improves performance but plateaus beyond ViT-L; text scaling is beneficial through Base-v1 in the reported ViT-L comparison but Large-v1 performs worse. The authors also describe overfitting and unstable training for Large-v1.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding Transformer layers to the mapping structure (1 to 4) does not improve and often hurts retrieval (WIT 34.1 to 29.0; Infoseek 42.7 to 40.8; Table 6).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling the cross-modal connector of a multimodal retriever does not improve retrieval performance.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (2024)
record.problems: The scaling results use retrieval metrics rather than held-out language-model loss and do not fit power laws. The paper reports that each model was reproduced once and gives run differences, but does not provide uncertainty estimates for the scaling comparisons. Scaling conclusions are specific to the reported model components and data.
record.rows_left_out: Other dataset-specific Table 2 metrics and additional ablations are not included; the extracted rows retain the reported average-rank size comparisons, the two explicitly stated ViT-B-to-ViT-G dataset comparisons, and the Stage 0 MSMARCO scaling results in Table 3.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No fits and no extrapolation to larger runs.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count. Mapping-layer depth (Table 6) adds parameters, so it is not a fixed-size shape test.
No power-law form is fitted for vision or multimodal retrievers.
Predictability in the sense of a fitted trend; the relation between pretraining loss and downstream performance; general LM benchmarks.
No exponents or fitting choices are compared.

missing.what: Stage 1 results for vision and text encoder scaling. Text encoder A.R. is 7.0/5.3/4.6/5.6 for Small/Medium/Base/Large-v1, so Large is already worse. ViT-G trails ViT-L on E-VQA (42.4 vs 45.0) and IGLUE after Stage 1.
Per-dataset Table 2 values for ViT-L to ViT-H to ViT-G (e.g. WIT 60.5/60.5/61.5; OVEN 59.8/61.5/63.4). These show the size of the plateau better than A.R. ranks do.
Fine-tuned single-task scaling from ViT-L to ViT-H to ViT-G (e.g. Infoseek 62.3 to 70.5 to 70.9 in the fine-tuned rows).

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3: this is a new setting, retrieval models built on pretrained encoders, rather than a different method on the LM question. Evidence for V6 is weak. There are only 3–4 sizes per axis, no fitted trend, single reported runs (best of two), and much of it uses Average Rank, a relative rank rather than an absolute metric. The vision-encoder rows concern ViT backbones, not language models, so linking them to V6 is a stretch; a researcher may prefer to weight only the text-encoder rows. The Large-v1 reversal coincides with training collapse fixed by LoRA, so it reflects the training regime as much as scale.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, and compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power-law fits on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter-token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The paper scales components of a multimodal retriever, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds in another modality or training regime.

The paper measures retrieval-task performance against encoder scale, but does not test general language-model downstream benchmarks or the relationship between pretraining loss and downstream performance.
No power-law exponents or compute-optimal allocations are fitted or compared.

relationships.condition: Text-only ColBERT-v1 retrieval on MSMARCO (Small to Large), and PreFLMR vision encoder scaled from ViT-B to ViT-L/ViT-G with text encoder fixed
relationships.reason: MRR@10 and Recall@50 rise monotonically with size (r2–r4, r6–r8). A.R. improves from ViT-B to ViT-L (r10), and Infoseek/E-VQA rise from ViT-B to ViT-G (r18, r20).
relationships.display_finding: MRR@10 and Recall@50 increased monotonically with size, while A.R. improved from ViT-B to ViT-L and Infoseek and E-VQA improved from ViT-B to ViT-G.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Text-only ColBERT-v1 retrieval on MSMARCO (Small to Large), and PreFLMR vision encoder scaled from ViT-B to ViT-L/ViT-G with text encoder fixed
source_check.reason: Table 3 shows monotonically improving MRR@10 and Recall@50 across text-encoder sizes (r2–r4, r6–r8). Table 2 shows better average rank from ViT-B to ViT-L (r10) and higher Infoseek and E-VQA PR@5 from ViT-B to ViT-G (r18, r20).

relationships.condition: Vision encoder beyond ViT-L; text encoder Small-v1 to Medium-v1 in the multimodal model
relationships.reason: Gains are negligible or small where size grows by about 2–6x: ViT-L to H to G plateaus (r11, r12), and Small to Medium text encoders barely move A.R. (r14).
relationships.display_finding: Increasing encoder size by about 2–6× yielded negligible or small gains, with vision performance plateauing beyond ViT-L and average recall barely changing from Small-v1 to Medium-v1.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Vision encoder beyond ViT-L; text encoder Small-v1 to Medium-v1 in the multimodal model
source_check.reason: The authors explicitly describe a vision-scaling plateau at ViT-H/G; task scores improve only modestly despite better average rank (r11, r12). Small-v1 to Medium-v1 changes average rank only from 8.3 to 8.2, with mixed task-level changes (r14). Together these qualify the scale-performance relationship.

relationships.condition: Multimodal PreFLMR with ViT-L, text encoder scaled from Base-v1 to Large-v1, on the available training data
relationships.reason: The larger text encoder performs worse (A.R. 5.6 to 6.6, r16). The authors attribute this to overfitting and unstable training, whereas the same scaling helps in text-only Stage 0.
relationships.display_finding: Average rank worsened from 5.6 to 6.6, which the authors attributed to overfitting and unstable training, although the same scaling helped during text-only training.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Multimodal PreFLMR with ViT-L, text encoder scaled from Base-v1 to Large-v1, on the available training data
source_check.reason: Average rank worsens from 5.6 to 6.6 with the larger text encoder (r16). Section 5.2 and Appendix B.3 attribute this to overfitting and unstable training; text-only Stage 0 instead benefits from Large-v1.

relation.reason: Its own controlled encoder-size comparisons bear directly on V6's relationship between scale and downstream retrieval performance.

tranche.reason: The study tests encoder-size scaling in a new setting, multimodal late-interaction retrieval, using retrieval performance rather than language-model pretraining loss.

source_check.notes: A.R. is a relative rank, not an absolute performance score. Appendix B.3 reports that Large-v1 required LoRA to stabilize training, limiting interpretation as a size-only comparison; these results establish scaling trends rather than a fitted predictive law.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ColBERT-v1 text retrieval at the reported MSMARCO sizes, and PreFLMR performance from ViT-B to ViT-G on Infoseek and E-VQA
reader_labels.reason: Larger ColBERT models have higher reported MRR@10 and Recall@50, and the ViT-G PreFLMR results exceed the ViT-B values on both named datasets (r2-r4, r6-r8, r18, r20).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: PreFLMR text-encoder scaling at ViT-L and vision scaling beyond ViT-L
reader_labels.reason: The Large-v1 text encoder has worse average rank than Base-v1, while the paper describes performance as plateauing at ViT-H and ViT-G; thus gains are not uniformly predictable from size alone (r11, r12, r16).
